data.narrative:
d-Matrix, a Series C semiconductor company founded by Sid Sheth and Sudeep Bhoja, entered this round at a $2.0B post-money valuation following $450M in cumulative fundraising. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set spanning 3 public semiconductor equities (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the chip design and AI acceleration space, including Tenstorrent, Positron AI, and DEEPX.

Two triangulation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression anchoring projects forward from the $2.0B Series C post-money using a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to a next-stage entry point, yielding $3.4B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Tenstorrent at $2.7B (Series D), Positron AI at $1.0B (Series B), and DEEPX at $529M (Series C)—produces a median of $1.0B, with a observed range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (21.0x median across the three public tickers) could not be applied due to the absence of revenue disclosure from d-Matrix.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a valuation range of $850M to $3.9B, with a median estimate of $2.2B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in peer staging and business maturity. Key uncertainties center on d-Matrix's revenue trajectory and competitive positioning within its cohort, neither of which the available data directly address.
